chunks: It is narrated that Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام said to a man from Bani Sa'd:

Shall I not tell you about myself and Fatimah al-Zahra'? She was with me, and she drew water with the waterskin until it left a mark on her chest, and she ground with the handmill until her hands blistered, and she swept the house until her clothes became dusty, and she kindled beneath the cooking pot until her clothes darkened. Great hardship afflicted her because of that, so I said to her: If only you would go to your father and ask him for a servant to spare you the hardship of what you are in of this work.

So she went to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and found people with him, so she felt shy and turned back. He صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم understood that she had come for some need, so he came to us in the morning while we were in our covering and said, 'Peace be upon you.' We remained silent and were shy because of our state. Then he said, 'Peace be upon you,' and we remained silent. Then he said, 'Peace be upon you,' and we feared that if we did not reply to him he would leave; and he used to do that, greeting three times, and if permission was given to him, otherwise he would leave. So we said, 'And upon you be peace, O Messenger of Allah, enter.' Then he entered and sat near our heads, and then said: 'O Fatimah, what was your need yesterday with Muhammad?'

So I feared that if we did not answer him, he would rise and leave. I brought out my head and said: By Allah, I will inform you, O Messenger of Allah. She drew water with the waterskin until it marked her chest, and turned the handmill until her hands blistered, and swept the house until her clothes became dusty, and kindled beneath the cooking pot until her clothes darkened. So I said to her: If only you would go to your father and ask him for a servant to spare you the hardship of what you are in of this work.

He said: 'Shall I not teach you both something better for you than a servant? When you take to your bed, then say Allahu Akbar thirty-four times, and Subhan Allah thirty-three times, and Al-hamdu li-llah thirty-three times.' Then Fatimah عليها السلام raised her head and said: 'I am pleased with Allah and with His Messenger; I am pleased with Allah and with His Messenger.'

key_terms.الرَّحَى: the handmill used for grinding grain
key_terms.الْقِرْبَةِ: the waterskin used for carrying water
key_terms.تَحْمِيدَةً: the saying of Al-hamdu li-llah in praise
key_terms.تَسْبِيحَةً: the saying of Subhan Allah in glorification
key_terms.خَادِمًا: a servant who would assist with labor

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم teach Fatimah عليها السلام instead of giving her a servant?
ai.summary: This hadith recounts the hardship borne by Fatimah al-Zahra' عليها السلام in household labor and the compassion of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم toward her and Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام. Instead of assigning a servant, he taught them a form of dhikr before sleep that is presented as better than worldly assistance. The narration is a foundational source for the well-known Tasbih of Fatimah عليها السلام.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.947 - It is narrated that The Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) said to a man from the Bani Sa'd tribe:
"Shall I tell you about myself and Sayyida Fatimah Al-Zahra {S.A}? She used to carry water with the water-skin until it left a mark on her chest. She ground grain with the millstone until her hands blistered. She swept the house until her clothes were covered in dust, and She kindled the fire under the cooking pot until her clothes were stained. She suffered greatly from these tasks. I said to her,
'Why don’t you go to your father and ask him for a servant to relieve you of the hardships of this work?'
She went to the Prophet but found him with people (guests), so She felt shy and left. The Prophet, realizing She had come for something, came to us the next morning while we were still in our beds.
He greeted us with 'Peace be upon you,' and we remained silent out of shyness.
He then said: 'Peace be upon you' again, and we still did not reply.
He repeated, 'Peace be upon you,' and we feared he would leave if we did not respond.
We then replied: 'And peace be upon you, O’ Messenger of Allah (sw), please enter.'
He came in and sat by our heads. He asked:
'O’ Sayyida Fatimah Al-Zahra {S.A}, what was your need yesterday with Muhammad?'
I was worried that if we did not answer, he would leave, so I said:
'I will tell you, O’ Messenger of Allah (sw). She carried water with the water-skin until it marked her chest, ground with the millstone until her hands blistered, swept until her clothes were dusty, and kindled fire until her clothes were stained. I suggested She ask you for a servant to ease her burdens.'
The Prophet replied: 'Shall I not teach you something better than a servant? When you go to bed, say Allahu Akbar (God is Great) thirty-four times, SubhanAllah (swt) (Glory be to God) thirty-three times, and Alhamdulillah (Praise be to God) thirty-three times.'
Sayyida Fatimah Al-Zahra {S.A} then lifted her head and said:
'I am content with Allah (swt) and His Messenger. I am content with Allah (swt) and His Messenger.'"
